title: Heavy Vehicle National Law commences (New South Wales)
summary: New South Wales applied the Heavy Vehicle National Law and its national regulations from 10 February 2014, with the National Heavy Vehicle Regulator administering access permits, accreditation and national fatigue, mass and dimension rules in place of separate state regimes.

instruments.title: Heavy Vehicle (Adoption of National Law) Act 2013 (NSW)
instruments.provisions: Applies the HVNL (schedule to the Qld Act) as a law of the jurisdiction

direction_rationale: A single national heavy-vehicle law and regulator replaces differing state rules, lowering compliance costs for interstate operators and easing expansion across borders.
comparison: Western Australia and Northern Territory (never adopted the HVNL)
notes: All six adopting jurisdictions share one date; identification relies on WA/NT controls. Application Act titles not individually confirmed on registers.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 14-15 October 2026 from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: One national heavy vehicle law and regulator replaced differing state rules on fatigue, mass, dimensions and access. It lowers compliance costs for interstate freight operators, though the law has been criticised as complex and access permits were slow at first.

marks.reason: A single national law and regulator replaced state-by-state rules for heavy vehicles.
Interstate operators deal with one set of rules and one regulator instead of several.

assessment.confidence_note: The archived econometric evaluation found no detectable effect on road freight entry or exit (grade Moderate). Western Australia and the Northern Territory are not in the scheme.
